<title>List of female Nobel laureates</title>
<fragment>

The most recent women to be awarded a Nobel Prize were Claudia Goldin in Economics, Narges Mohammadi for Peace, Anne L'Huillier in Physics and Katalin Karikó in Physiology or Medicine (2023), Annie Ernaux in Literature and Carolyn R. Bertozzi for Chemistry (2022), Maria Ressa for Peace (2021), Louise Glück in Literature, Andrea M. Ghez in Physics, Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer A. Doudna in Chemistry (2020), and Esther Duflo in Economics (2019).




## Female laureates

[edit]

* Physiology or Medicine
* Physics

* Economic Sciences

* Alan Asaid (26 September 2009). "Så ratade Akademien kvinnorna" [How the Academy Rejected the Women]. *SvD* (in Swedish).

</fragment>
<fragment>

As of 2023, 65 Nobel Prizes and the Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences have been awarded to 64 women.[1][3] Unique Nobel Prize laureates include 894 men, 60 women, and 27 organizations.[4]


The distribution of Nobel prizes awarded to women is as follows:



* nineteen women have won the Nobel Peace Prize (16.3% of 110 awarded);[5]
* seventeen have won the Nobel Prize in Literature (14.28% of 119 awarded);[6]
* thirteen have won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (5.6% of 230 awarded);[7]
* eight have won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry (4.1% of 191 awarded);[8]
* five have won the Nobel Prize in Physics (1.8% of 224 awarded);[9]
* and three (Elinor Ostrom, Esther Duflo and Claudia Goldin) have won the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences (2.17% of 92 awarded).[10]


</fragment>
</document>

Responding by telephone to the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, Duflo explained that she received the prize "at an extremely opportune and important time" and hoped that it would "inspire many, many other women to continue working and many other men to give them the respect that they deserve, like every single human being."[44] She also revealed that she wanted to use the award as a "megaphone" in her fighting efforts to tackle poverty and to improve children's education.[45]


French President Emmanuel Macron offered his congratulations: "Esther Duflo's magnificent Nobel Prize is a reminder that French economists are currently among the best in the world and shows that research in that field can have concrete impact on human welfare."[46]

Based on my research, here are the female winners of the Nobel Prize in 2019 and 2020:

## 2019
- **Esther Duflo** - Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences (along with Abhijit Banerjee and Michael Kremer for their experimental approach to alleviating global poverty)

## 2020
Four female Nobel Prize winners in 2020:

- **Emmanuelle Charpentier** - Nobel Prize in Chemistry (along with Jennifer Doudna for the development of the CRISPR-Cas9 genetic scissors method)
- **Jennifer Doudna** - Nobel Prize in Chemistry (along with Emmanuelle Charpentier for the development of the CRISPR-Cas9 genetic scissors method)
- **Louise Glück** - Nobel Prize in Literature (for her unmistakable poetic voice that with austere beauty makes individual existence universal)
- **Andrea M. Ghez** - Nobel Prize in Physics (along with Roger Penrose and Reinhard Genzel for the discovery of a supermassive compact object at the centre of our galaxy)

In summary, there was **1 female Nobel laureate in 2019** and **4 female Nobel laureates in 2020**, making a total of **5 female winners** across these two years.
